"""A partial spelling-and-format approximation.

Negative rules match split b/m onsets and selected following letter classes.
Positive rules match Indonesian-looking prefixes after function-word cues,
split Thai มี / เป็น, and Vietnamese có. Opening punctuation and module
keyword prefixes have separate estimates, as does middle-dot-only filler.
State resets at document boundaries. Finer lexical variation is omitted.
"""
from anyascii import anyascii
from functools import lru_cache
READS = ()

INDONESIAN = frozenset(('yang', 'dan', 'dengan', 'untuk', 'tidak', 'dalam',
                       'dari', 'akan', 'pada', 'ini', 'itu', 'juga', 'dapat',
                       'tersebut', 'saja', 'bisa', 'oleh', 'adalah', 'mereka'))
VERB_PREFIXES = ('mem', 'men', 'mel', 'meng', 'ber', 'ter', 'per', 'pen')
VOWELS = frozenset('aeiou')

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def spelling(text):
    return anyascii(text).lower()


def opening(text, s):
    word = s.lstrip()
    value = -.104
    if not word:
        return value - .051
    if s[0].isspace(): value += .069
    if word[0].isdigit():
        value -= .111
    elif word[0].isalpha():
        if text.lstrip()[0].isupper(): value -= .043
        if word.startswith(('import', 'package', 'include', 'using', 'require')):
            value += .618
    else:
        value += .053
        for chars, adjustment in [('#', .538), ('/', .167), ('\\', -.144),
                                  ('.', -.140), ('([{', -.146),
                                  ('\"\'', -.122)]:
            if word[0] in chars: value += adjustment
    if text == ' .': return -1.6
    if text == '\\': return -1.17
    if '\n' in text and text.strip() == '//': return 3.18
    if word.startswith('//'): value += .444
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous, language, dots_only = (
        ('', 0., True) if first else carry[1:]
    )
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s, p = spelling(text), spelling(previous).lstrip()
    if text.startswith('<|'): language = 0.
    if text.strip().lower() in INDONESIAN:
        language = min(10., language + 1.)
    else:
        language *= .996
    value = -.001
    if first: value += opening(text, s)
    continuation = bool(s) and s[0].isalpha() and not s[0].isspace()
    if continuation and p == 'b':
        if s[0] in 'bm': value -= .55
        if len(s) > 1 and s[0] in 'bmr' and s[1] in 'ei':
            value -= .65
        if len(s) > 1 and all(c in VOWELS for c in s[:2]):
            value -= .13
    if continuation and p == 'm' and s[0] in 'iy': value -= .06
    if language >= .7:
        if s.lstrip().startswith(VERB_PREFIXES):
            value += .4
            if s.lstrip().startswith(('mem', 'men')): value += .575
        if continuation and p.startswith(VERB_PREFIXES): value += .476
    if text == 'ี' and previous.rstrip().endswith('ม'): value += 4.5
    if text == '็น' and previous.rstrip().endswith('เป'): value += 1.15
    if text.strip().lower() == 'có': value += .74
    dots_only = (dots_only and bool(text.strip())
                 and set(text.strip()) == {'·'})
    if dots_only: value = -.45 if first else -.668
    return (doc, text, language, dots_only), value

In plain terms: the component is positive in text about building, implementing or writing
something (code, a script, an application, an example, a project). Its main triggers are
making-words ("implement", "create", "make", "write", "build", "code", ...). Those words are

slightly below zero.

"""Recognize category-head nouns in identifying phrases.

The main signal is negative on a common head after a content-word modifier:
`the X method`, `the X family`, `the X industry`. Capitalization, rarity,
and relational adjectives estimate how identifying the modifier is. A
nearby `the` strengthens the signal. Unmodified words get zero.
Other dictionary nouns get a small fallback;
city/island/sea labels get a positive signal. Noun-following emphatic
reflexives get a negative signal. Head groups share weights, so this does
not reproduce individual phrases' full activation peaks.

import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

SOCIAL_DOMAINS = frozenset('''
family community people tribe race population industry sector economy market
profession world scene movement team genre
'''.split())
FORMAL_TERMS = frozenset('''
method model system theory theorem conjecture concept principle formula
equation algorithm sequence distribution function relation rule law property
problem mechanism pattern framework scheme protocol hierarchy structure
class module library tensor inequality spectrum plane curve rate table flag
parameter variable field
'''.split())
ORGANIZATIONS = frozenset('''
group company corporation society association foundation committee council
parliament congress assembly government administration organization union party
army police department ministry university institute bureau board agency
empire league partnership trust
'''.split())
FEATURES_AND_EVENTS = frozenset('''
process operation procedure effect cycle phase force pathway experience
case factor side axis direction level penalty war campaign award awards
festival games election era period season crisis pandemic
'''.split())
PLACES = frozenset('''
district region province river valley mountains range canal railway area
peninsula campus hotel highway arena trail
'''.split())
MEDIA_AND_SOFTWARE = frozenset('''
language program programme project plan task code website page interface
business package tool object format version
'''.split())
BIOLOGICAL_TYPES = frozenset('''
gene protein virus receptor vaccine disease syndrome genome
'''.split())

FUNCTION = frozenset('''
a an the this that these those any some no each every all both either neither
my your his her its our their whose which what such same other own another
of to in on at by for from with as and or but than is was be been being
have has had do does did will would can could shall should may might must
it they we you he she i not very more most less least only also one two
'''.split())

GROUPS = (SOCIAL_DOMAINS, FORMAL_TERMS, ORGANIZATIONS,
          FEATURES_AND_EVENTS, PLACES, MEDIA_AND_SOFTWARE | BIOLOGICAL_TYPES)
WEIGHTS = (-0.18, -0.13, -0.07, -0.13, -0.13, -0.08, 0.10, -0.01)

@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def head_group(word):
    for group, words in enumerate(GROUPS):
        if word in words:
            return group
    if word in {'city', 'island', 'sea'}:
        return 6
    if word not in FUNCTION and 'noun' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word):
        return 7
    return -1

@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def modifier(word):
    """A named or classifying modifier is stronger than a descriptive one."""
    lower = word.lower()
    if lower in FUNCTION:
        return 0.0
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(lower)
    relational = 'adj.pert' in wordnet.categories(lower, 'adjective')
    rarity = max(0.0, 4.0 - zipf_frequency(lower, 'en'))
    code_or_number = any(ch.isdigit() or ch in '_#.' for ch in word)
    return (0.36 + 0.58 * ('noun' in pos) + 0.69 * relational
            + word[:1].isupper() + 0.31 * rarity
            - 0.37 * code_or_number + 0.64 * (not pos))


def phrase_signal(tail, token):
    """Return the kind of head and its modifier/definiteness strength."""
    if token.startswith((' ', '-')) and token[1:].isalpha():
        word, before = token[1:], tail
    elif token.isascii() and token.isalpha():
        # A word may finish across several tokenizer pieces.
        joined = tail + token
        match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)$', joined)
        word, before = match.group(1), joined[:match.start()].rstrip()
    else:
        return -1, 0.0
    if not word.isascii():
        return -1, 0.0
    group = head_group(word.lower())
    if group < 0:
        return -1, 0.0
    match = re.search(r"(\w[\w#.'-]*)[`\"()]*$", before)
    if not match:
        return group, 0.0
    strength = modifier(match.group(1))
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9'-]+", before.lower())[-7:]
    boundaries = [w for w in words if w in FUNCTION]
    definite = bool(boundaries and boundaries[-1] == 'the')
    return group, strength * (4.55 if definite else 1.0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    group, strength = phrase_signal(tail, token)
    value = WEIGHTS[group] * strength if group >= 0 else 0.0
    if token in (' itself', ' themselves'):
        match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)$', tail)
        if match and 'noun' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(match.group(1)):
            value = -0.97
    return (doc, (tail + token)[-120:]), float(value)

"""Backtick-storm detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1326 (layer 1, MLP).

The component is silent on almost all text. Its large responses come from three
concrete situations.

1. Backtick storm (strong, negative). Code that has been pasted with a backtick
   around its tokens, and with non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) used for indentation,
   e.g. "\\xa0``for` `i ``in` `range``(`". On a backtick token (a bare ` or ``,
   with or without a leading space; triple-backtick fences are ignored), if the
   last 32 tokens of the same document contain at least 2 other backtick tokens
   and at least 1 non-breaking space, the activation is about -4.5. It is about
   -9.8 for a space-prefixed double backtick " ``", and about -1.5 when the
   backtick is glued to punctuation (e.g. "}`"). Ordinary inline code, such as
   "`A`, `AAAA`", has few backticks in a row and no non-breaking spaces, so it
   stays at 0.

2. Document-start "Title:" (strong, positive). The colon in "Title:" right after
   an end-of-text token, the start of a new web page, is about +8.2.

3. Chinese education and test words (weak, positive). 教育 (education) about +2.3,
   its second character 育 about +1.5, and 验 (as in 测验, a test) about +2.2.

tokens' backtick and non-breaking-space flags), so it needs no other component.

READS = ()

WINDOW = 32
END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"
EDUCATION_WORDS = {"教育": 2.3, "育": 1.5, "验": 2.2}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        recent = []  # a new document starts with no history
    else:
        recent = carry[1]

    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    is_tick = "`" in text and "```" not in text
    is_nbsp = "\xa0" in text
    n_ticks = sum(tick for tick, _ in recent)
    n_nbsp = sum(nbsp for _, nbsp in recent)

    value = EDUCATION_WORDS.get(text, 0.0)
    if is_tick and n_ticks >= 2 and n_nbsp >= 1:
        if text == " ``":
            value = -9.8
        elif text.strip() in ("`", "``"):
            value = -4.5
        else:
            value = -1.5
    if text == ":" and len(prefix.token_strings) >= 3:
        if prefix.token_strings[-2] == "Title" and prefix.token_strings[-3] == END_OF_TEXT:
            value = 8.2

    new_recent = (recent + [(is_tick, is_nbsp)])[-WINDOW:]
    return (doc, new_recent), value

"""Approximate a negative response to institutional names and initialisms.

Capitalization and word frequency provide a weak abbreviation cue. Dictionary
classes identify agencies, public bodies and universities more confidently.
Nearby title words, expanded initials, legal codes and institutional domains
add evidence. Chinese institutions use dictionary glosses and agency suffixes.
This captures a category, not the different strength of every individual name.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import cedict
import regex
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

# Technical abbreviations are not, by themselves, institution names.
COMPUTING = frozenset('''
API HTTP HTTPS HTML CSS JSON XML SQL CPU GPU RAM ROM USB UTF ASCII
URL URI TCP UDP SSL TLS DNS CLI GUI SDK CSV PDF PHP YAML SVG
RGB GB MB KB JPEG PNG GIF BIOS FTP SSH RSA AES ID IP ISBN ISSN
'''.split())
HEADS = frozenset('''
association society organization organisation federation commission council
committee agency union club bureau board
'''.split())
OFFICIAL = {'royal', 'national', 'international', 'american', 'world', 'federal'}
PORTFOLIOS = frozenset('''
defense defence education commerce treasury energy labor labour justice
agriculture interior transportation health affairs state
'''.split())
CIVIC_NAMES = (
    'White House', 'Federal Reserve', 'Court of Appeals', 'Veterans Affairs',
    'United Nations', 'World Bank', 'European Union', 'Red Cross',
)
INSTITUTION_OF = re.compile(
    r'(?:University|Institute|Department|Ministry|Secretary|College|Academy|'
    r'Institutes) (?:of|for)(?: [A-Z][a-z]+)?$'
)

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def classes(word):
    w = word.lower()
    org = wordnet.is_a(w, 'organization') and not wordnet.is_a(w, 'country')
    university = wordnet.is_a(w, 'university') or wordnet.is_a(w, 'college')
    known = org or university or wordnet.is_a(w, 'institution')
    ordinary = bool(wordnet.parts_of_speech(w)) and not known
    agency = (wordnet.is_a(w, 'government agency') or
              wordnet.is_a(w, 'government department'))
    public = any(wordnet.is_a(w, k) for k in (
        'world organization', 'pressure group', 'professional association'))
    categories = wordnet.categories(w)
    specific = ('noun.group' in categories and
                categories <= {'noun.group', 'noun.substance', 'noun.animal'})
    body = any(wordnet.is_a(w, k) for k in (
        'association', 'society', 'federation', 'legislature'))
    named_university = university and w not in {'university', 'college', 'school'}
    return known, ordinary, agency, public, specific, body, named_university

@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def chinese_institution(text):
    for length in range(2, min(len(text), 6) + 1):
        gloss = ' '.join(cedict.glosses(text[-length:])).lower()
        if any(k in gloss for k in (
            'ministry', 'committee', 'commission', 'academy', 'university',
            'association', 'federation', 'news agency')):
            return True
    return False


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (tail + s)[-180:]
    value = 0.0
    match = regex.search(r'[\p{Lu}\p{Ll}]+(?:\.[\p{Lu}\p{Ll}]+)*$', text)
    word = match.group().replace('.', '') if match else ''
    if (word.isupper() and 2 <= len(word) <= 12
            and any(c.isalpha() for c in s)):
        known, ordinary, agency, public, specific, _, _ = classes(word)
        language = 'ru' if regex.search(r'\p{Cyrillic}', word) else 'en'
        band = min(6, int(zipf_frequency(word, language)))
        continuing = bool(tail) and tail[-1].isalpha() and not s[:1].isspace()
        if word not in COMPUTING:
            if ordinary and len(word) >= 3:
                curve = (0, -.14, -.18, -.07, 0, 0, 0)
            elif continuing:
                curve = (-.13, -.30, -.25, -.25, -.10, 0, .10)
            else:
                curve = (0, 0, -.10, -.13, 0, 0, 0)
            value += curve[band]
        if known:
            value -= .54 * (len(word) >= 3 and agency)
            value -= .44 * public
            value -= .59 * (len(word) >= 3 and specific)
        # Matching initials in nearby title-cased words suggest an expansion.
        paren = max(text.rfind('('), text.rfind('（'))
        if paren >= 0 and text[paren+1:].replace('.', '').isupper():
            initials = ''.join(w[0] for w in re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', text[:paren])
                               if w.istitle())
            if word in initials:
                value -= .46
        if word in {'USC', 'USCA', 'CFR'}:
            value -= 1.54
    token = s.strip()
    if token.istitle() and token.isalpha() and len(token) > 2:
        known, _, _, _, _, body, university = classes(token)
        words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', tail)
        previous_title = bool(words and words[-1].istitle())
        value -= .29 * university + .09 * body
        if token.lower() in HEADS:

        if known and any(w.lower() in OFFICIAL for w in words[-3:]):
            value -= .36
        if INSTITUTION_OF.search(tail):
            value -= .25 + .56 * (token.lower() in PORTFOLIOS)

        value -= .89
    if token == '.org':

    if any(text.endswith(name) for name in CIVIC_NAMES):
        value -= .98
    if token in {'委', '厅', '廳'}:
        value -= .85

                       '出版社', '教育部', '教育局', '教育厅')):
        value -= .17
    han = regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}+$', text)
    if han and chinese_institution(han.group()[-8:]):
        value -= .30
    return (doc, text), float(value)

  * A few rare patterns are included because they are among its largest values: a run

2. Every document's first token gets a small, mostly negative value (about -0.14 on
   average). The exact value depends on which token it is, and no simple word class
   captures that, so this program uses the average.

Everywhere else it predicts 0. Ordinary text gives small values with no clear pattern,
which this program does not try to capture.
"""

READS = ()

SPIKE = 11.7          # the "Title:" colon at a document start
FIRST_TOKEN = -0.14   # average activation on a document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (previous token's text, whether the previous token opened its document)
    prev_text, prev_opened = carry if carry is not None else (None, False)
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    opens = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if opens:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN
    elif text == ":" and prev_text == "Title" and prev_opened:
        value = SPIKE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (text, opens), value

"""Bare-space detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 1338.

This component fires on a standalone " " token: a space the tokenizer emitted
on its own. In this model's text that is almost always the space before a
number ("by 3", "after 25 minutes", "of 2010"), because digits are split one
per token and the space before them gets its own token. The program sees only
the prefix, so it cannot see the number; it reads the token before the space.
The size depends on what precedes the space:

  * after a word (a letter)          -> strong, about 0.9
  * after an operator or colon       -> medium, about 0.6   ("= ", ": ", "+ ")
  * after a full stop                -> weak, about 0.4
  * after a comma                    -> weak, about 0.2
  * after a digit, after whitespace, or at the start of a document -> 0
    (runs of spaces, indentation and "0 0 0"-style lists do not fire)

A second, smaller effect: the first token of each document (or of a row) is
pushed negative, about -0.3, since the model has no earlier context there.
All other tokens give 0; their activations are small and noisy.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

DOC_START = -0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(toks) == 1 or docs[-2] != docs[-1]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if toks[-1] != " ":
        return carry, 0.0
    end = toks[-2][-1:]
    if end.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.9
    if end in ("=", "+", "-", "/", ":", ";"):
        return carry, 0.6
    if end == ".":
        return carry, 0.4
    if end == ",":
        return carry, 0.2
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 1339: an "intense or large amount" detector.

The component fires (positive, sometimes strongly) on the last piece of a word or phrase
that expresses something very large, very many, or very much. Cases, with typical
activations:

- Romance superlatives -issimo / -issima / -ísimo / -ísima ("bellissimo", "dificilísima"): ~7-9
- "over N" after a number, Chinese 多 / 余 / 几 / 幾 ("60多岁", "400余", "二十几"): ~6
- "N+" with no space ("30+", "100+"): ~2
- "N%" after 100 ("100%"): ~2.4
- decades: the "s" of "1940s" (~3) and "80s" (~1.4)
- "of" after a quantity word: "tens of" (~7), "hundreds of" (~5),
  "thousands of" (~2.5), "lots of" (~2.3)
- "numer-ous", "countless", "nombre-uses" (many / numerous);
  Spanish -oso / -osa adjectives (~2.5)
- "one hundred and ..." (~5), "every single" (~6)

Everything else predicts 0. The rules are calibrated on the mean activation of each case
in training text. The program reads only the current token, the text up to it, and the
token before it, so it needs no state and is causal.
"""
READS = ()
import re

# How strongly "of" fires after a quantity word.
OF_AFTER = {"tens": 6.5, "hundreds": 5.0, "dozens": 3.0, "thousands": 2.5, "lots": 2.3,
            "loads": 2.3, "tons": 2.3, "ton": 2.0, "millions": 1.5, "billions": 1.5, "full": 1.2}
# Latin-script words meaning "very many"; the last piece fires.
MANY_WORDS = {"numerous", "countless", "innumerable", "nombreuses", "nombreux", "nombreuse",
              "zahlreiche", "numerosos", "numerosas"}
# Chinese characters meaning "more than" when they follow a number.
OVER_CHARS = set("多余几幾来來餘余")
NUMBER_CHARS = "0-9〇零一二三四五六七八九十百千万亿两"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    # The word the current token completes, and the word just before it.
    word = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]+$", text)
    word = word.group(0).lower() if word else ""
    prev_word = re.search(r"([^\W\d_]+)\W*$", before)
    prev_word = prev_word.group(1).lower() if prev_word else ""
    # The number the current token follows, if any, and the character before that number.
    number = re.search(f"([{NUMBER_CHARS}]+)$", before)
    number = number.group(1) if number else ""
    before_number = before[: len(before) - len(number)] if number else ""

    value = 0.0
    if re.search(r"(iss|íss|ís)[ií]m[oaie]?s?$", word):
        value = 7.0  # Romance superlative: -issimo, -ísima
    elif ("多" in cur or cur in OVER_CHARS) and number:
        value = 6.0  # "over N"
    elif cur.strip() in ("s", "'s", "’s") and number.endswith("0") and len(number) == 4:
        value = 3.1  # decade, 1940s
    elif cur.strip() in ("s", "'s", "’s") and number.endswith("0") and len(number) == 2:
        value = 1.35  # decade, 80s
    elif cur.startswith(("-plus", "plus")) and number:
        value = 4.0  # 10,000-plus
    elif cur == "+" and len(number) >= 2 and before_number[-1:] in ("", " ", "\n"):
        value = 2.0  # 30+
    elif cur == "%" and before.endswith("100"):
        value = 2.4  # 100%
    elif cur.lower() == " of" and prev_word in OF_AFTER:
        value = OF_AFTER[prev_word]  # tens of, thousands of
    elif word in MANY_WORDS and not cur.startswith(" "):
        value = 3.0  # numer-ous, nombre-uses
    elif cur == " and" and prev_word in {"hundred", "thousand"}:
        value = 5.0  # one hundred and
    elif cur == " single" and prev_word == "every":
        value = 6.0  # every single
    elif not cur.startswith(" ") and re.search(r"(oso|osa|osos|osas)$", word):
        value = 2.5  # Spanish -oso / -osa adjectives
    elif not cur.startswith(" ") and re.search(r"ous$", word):
        value = 0.4  # other -ous adjectives
    return carry, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1342: the adverb-ending component.

What it does: it switches on at the token that completes an -ly adverb. It responds most to
comment adverbs that open or qualify a whole statement ("Interestingly,", "Unfortunately,",
"Accordingly,", "Obviously,", "Surprisingly,", "Sadly,"), and to -ingly / -edly adverbs
generally. Other -ly adverbs ("completely", "trivially") get a weak response, and
Spanish/Italian -mente adverbs a modest one. It stays near 0 on everything else, including
connectives (however, therefore, also), order and time adverbs (finally, firstly,
alternatively), degree and frequency adverbs (only, especially, highly, usually), and
-ly adjectives (family, early, supply, friendly).

How it works: take the word that ends at the current token (its letters, from the last
token that starts with a space or punctuation), and score it by the rules above. It reads
only the tokens so far and keeps no state.

What it leaves out: the activation is spread thinly over many other tokens, and the
rules capture only about 13% of its variance on eval rows.
"""
READS = ()

# Comment adverbs: they judge or link the whole statement.
COMMENT = {
    "interestingly", "unfortunately", "fortunately", "surprisingly", "sadly", "importantly",
    "notably", "obviously", "apparently", "clearly", "hopefully", "presumably", "admittedly",
    "remarkably", "unexpectedly", "accordingly", "consequently", "luckily", "happily",
    "thankfully", "regrettably", "ironically", "predictably", "understandably", "honestly",
    "frankly", "evidently", "reportedly", "allegedly", "undoubtedly", "doubtless",
    "incidentally", "conveniently", "tellingly", "curiously", "strangely", "oddly",
}
# -ly words that are not adverbs, or are adverbs of order, time or degree.
NOT_ADVERB = {"only", "family", "early", "likely", "july", "italy", "holy", "belly", "reply",
              "apply", "supply", "assembly", "butterfly", "anomaly", "molly", "polly", "emily",
              "kelly", "lovely", "friendly", "silly", "ugly", "rely", "multiply", "comply",
              "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "yearly", "elderly", "jelly", "curly"}
NOT_MANNER = {"alternatively", "additionally", "finally", "actually", "currently", "specifically",
              "especially", "particularly", "generally", "mostly", "mainly", "usually",
              "typically", "highly", "namely", "similarly", "firstly", "secondly", "thirdly",
              "lastly", "originally", "previously", "recently", "directly", "exactly", "really",
              "extremely", "simply", "merely", "partly", "closely", "probably", "certainly"}

# Activation levels for each kind of adverb (the component's own units).
COMMENT_LEVEL = 2.4    # comment adverbs, and -ingly / -edly adverbs
MENTE_LEVEL = 0.6      # Spanish / Italian -mente adverbs
OTHER_LY_LEVEL = 0.3   # any other -ly adverb


def _word(strings):
    """Letters of the word that ends at the current token, lowercased."""
    out = ""
    for i in range(len(strings) - 1, max(-1, len(strings) - 31), -1):
        piece = strings[i]
        out = piece + out
        if piece[:1] and not piece[0].isalpha():  # a space or punctuation starts the word
            break
    return "".join(c for c in out if c.isalpha()).lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings)
    if word in COMMENT or word.endswith(("ingly", "edly")):
        return None, COMMENT_LEVEL
    if word.endswith("mente") and len(word) > 6:
        return None, MENTE_LEVEL
    if len(word) >= 5 and word.endswith("ly") and not (word in NOT_ADVERB or word in NOT_MANNER):
        return None, OTHER_LY_LEVEL
    return None, 0.0
